claim: Experts sort problems by principle and novices by surface in the founding small study, but the original paper was never opened here; its numbers are known only through replications (8 vs 8 sorters). Update: the small-study design (8 vs 8) is now described in print by Wolf et al. 2012 (d03).
agent_test: none

claim: A large classroom replication (403 intro students, 21 grad students, 7 faculty) found intro students far less surface-bound than Chi's novices; calculus-based students overlapped grad students. The sharp novice/expert split is weaker than the textbook story. Update: a crossed-feature biology design with 23 faculty and 101 non-majors does show a wide gap (deep pairs 71.7% vs 29.2%), but that is an extreme-group contrast, not intro students.
agent_test: none

claim: Card-sort outcomes depend heavily on which problems are in the set. Some 5- and 10-problem subsets separate experts and novices almost totally, others not at all; natural textbook sets gave no clear conclusion while designed crossed-feature sets agreed with Chi.
agent_test: If the S0 gate classifies problem type, test it on crossed surface x principle items, not natural ones.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Much of the variation between human sorters is style (stacker vs spreader), not expertise; simple counts of categories do not separate experts from novices.
agent_test: none

claim: Who counts as expert changes the result: faculty sort better than PhD students, and graduate students overestimate how well students sort.
agent_test: none

claim: Mathematics replicates the sorting finding: professors sort by mathematical principle, undergraduates by surface; better school solvers sort more by structure (Schoenfeld and Herrmann 9 profs vs 19 students, strong-agreement pairs 10 vs 4).
agent_test: Have the agent sort a mixed math item set by principle; compare its groups to professor groups from the paper.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Sorting by deep structure can be trained but training the sort does not necessarily improve solving: a term-long course moved sorting toward experts, while 5 hours with a principle-first tool raised categorization yet not solving beyond controls. Update: in biology a revealed framework lifted novices only about 10 points (29.2 to 39.6% deep pairs) and advanced majors sorted like experts only after the framework was shown, so cueing differs from knowing.
agent_test: Compare scaffold with principle-naming step against no step at equal tokens; measure both sort quality and accuracy.

claim: Even experts are pulled by surface similarity, and novices who attempt principle-based reasoning solve more, even when the principle is wrongly named about 38% of the time.
agent_test: Compare forced principle-naming versus free solving on items with surface lures.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs are pulled by irrelevant surface content: one irrelevant sentence cuts GSM8K-style accuracy (GSM-IC macro under 30%; GSM-NoOp drops up to 65.7 points, GPT-4o -32.0, o1-preview -17.5). Update 2026: the effect is real but smaller in absolute size for reasoning models. Searched cat-trigger on R1 moved error from 1.50% to 4.50%; Claude Haiku 4.5 lost 1.3 points on GSM-Symbolic name/number variants; reasoning models pay 1.5x to 3x tokens under distraction.
agent_test: Add distractor-laden variants to the benchmark; test an explicit restate-and-filter step.

claim: Telling the model to ignore irrelevant information, adding distractor exemplars, or self-consistency each help but none close the gap; 8 same-question shots do not repair NoOp.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of ignore-instruction vs sampling.

claim: Prompting for the governing principle first (Step-Back) raised MMLU physics/chemistry (PaLM-2L 66.4 to 73.2; GPT-4 69.4 to 84.5, CoT 82.9) but fixes 20.5% of errors while adding 11.9% new ones; over 90% of remaining errors are in reasoning, not principle retrieval. Update: no test of Step-Back on reasoning models was found; plain CoT prompting adds only marginal accuracy for o3-mini, o4-mini and Gemini Flash 2.5 on GPQA Diamond (d10), so a small ceiling is expected.
agent_test: Test principle-first against CoT at equal tokens on items where deep structure is hidden.

claim: Skill- or template-indexed retrieval beats random or topic-based exemplars: skill labels +11.6 over CoT on MATH (42.2 to 53.88), +3.5 over topic-based; Buffer of Thoughts Game of 24 82.4; ReasonFlux 500 templates. Update: on AIME, curated abstract memory beat raw similarity retrieval (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 2024: 50.0 vs 43.3 vs 23.3 baseline) but on only 30 questions and with a strong instruction-only control (36.7).
agent_test: Memory keyed by problem-class label vs surface similarity retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Self-generated analogs and self-composed structures help moderately: analogical prompting GSM8K 76.7 to 77.8 on GPT-3.5, Self-Discover BBH 60 to 67; structures transfer across models.
agent_test: Compare self-generated related problems vs retrieved ones.

claim: LLMs rely on surface similarity in analogy: far-analogy GPT-4 39.6% (chance 50%) in ARN; counterfactual alphabets humans 75.3% vs GPT-3.5 35.0%; story analogies GPT-3 weaker than students.
agent_test: Use far-analogy retrieval probes for memory.

claim: Mechanistic and causal studies suggest models do abstract schema: entity probe accuracy falls to chance by layer 22 in Llama-3.3-70B; deep-structure causal effect is positive and grows with accuracy, closed models more than open. This conflicts with the pure pattern-matching reading.
agent_test: none

claim: Question syntax matters: rephrasing failed questions with the syntax of solved ones recovers answers (GSM8K Gemma-7B 37.76 to 46.02) and premise order changes accuracy by over 30%.
agent_test: Add a restate-in-canonical-form step and measure at equal tokens.

claim: Expert-persona prompts do not reliably improve accuracy: 162 personas on 2,410 MMLU questions mostly no significant effect, in-domain coefficient 0.004; expert identity wins only on judge-rated open answers.
agent_test: Do not add a persona; check skip.

claim: Only one LLM card sort in the Chi style was found: GPT-5 Thinking sorted 60 exam items by solution similarity into topic-and-solution-method groups, not surface groups (single author, one run, no human baseline, no link to solve accuracy).
agent_test: Run it: have the agent sort the Mason-Singh 25 problems and compare.

claim: Higher-level structure labels are not free: self-labelled skills work when produced by a strong model and transfer to weaker ones (GSM8K GPT-3.5 Retrieval-RSD 76.8 vs skill 82.03).
agent_test: Strong model labels, weak model uses.

claim: A frontier thinking model told to sort physics items by solution similarity did not sort by surface; whether sort quality predicts solve accuracy item by item is still untested, and exam items solved at 89-96% leave no room to test it.
agent_test: Use hard items (model fails about half) from a crossed surface-by-principle set; sort first, then solve, then correlate per item.

claim: Human card-sort results depend on style and on item design: stackers versus spreaders explain more variance than expertise, and only crossed-feature sets (Veldhuis sets 3-4, the biology task) give a clean split.
agent_test: Build a crossed set; report group count and double-filing for the agent.

claim: Outside physics, a crossed design with large samples reproduces the expert-novice sorting gap: biology faculty (n=23) 71.7% deep pairs vs non-majors (n=101) 29.2%; entering and advanced majors did not differ in free sort.
agent_test: Keep the sorting gap as a human fact; do not assume it holds for intro students.

claim: On hard math, abstracting a strategy into memory beat retrieving the raw similar case (AIME 2024 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 50.0 vs 43.3, 30 questions each), and uncurated full history hurt (26.7). Small samples, old models, tokens not matched; skill-keyed versus surface-keyed retrieval was not compared directly.
agent_test: Run skill-key vs surface-key retrieval on 100+ hard items at matched tokens.

claim: Adversarial irrelevant triggers raise reasoning-model error several-fold in relative terms but from low bases (R1 1.50% to 4.50%), and raise length (R1: 28.0% of answers over 1.5x tokens). Structured distractor flagging recovers accuracy at fewer tokens only after fine-tuning (DAGGER 359 vs 3,128 tokens).
agent_test: Test a prompt-only canonical-form step on a current reasoning model with token counts.

claim: The GSM-Symbolic drop is weaker than first reported: only 8 of 20 open models show significant drops, integer size shifted (K-S 0.12), and Claude Haiku 4.5 lost 1.3 points. GSM1k shows overfit mainly in open small families, not GPT, Gemini or Claude families.
agent_test: Rely on NoOp and distractor results, not the name/number variant, and check fresh-set controls for open models.

claim: In physics, most first errors of strong models are in deriving or applying relations (79-96% of first errors), not in reading the scenario (4-21%); wrong conservation-law assumptions are an example. The rate of wrongly named principle versus none was not measured.
agent_test: Log named principle and its correctness per attempt; compare wrong-named, none and right-named.
